motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one curve: exponential ease-out for every step-in.

motion.name: step
motion.purpose: Page transitions (fade + 2.5% rise), index numeral swap (fade + 25% slide from right), code strip reveal (fade + grow from left).

motion.name: arc-glide
motion.purpose: Progress arc easing between progress reports.

motion.name: record-breath
motion.purpose: Polar burst and arc scan head while recording.

motion.name: reduce-motion
motion.value: duration 0; transitions return the child; breath stopped at rest
motion.purpose: Applied whenever the platform disables animations.

breakpoints.purpose: Plot | writing side by side over a shared status/Record band, 11:10.

narrative.overview:
The studio is a record catalogue printed on a matte black sleeve. Each song is a numbered entry (LRS-001 and on). Its face is a polar pulse plot of its own waveform, and it carries a five-block colour code derived from its seed. The interface is set like a post-punk catalogue back cover: white hairline rules divide the page into bands, engraved mono capitals name things, and a plain light grotesk carries the words people write. There are no cards, no chrome and no Material furniture. Every control is a hairline-framed cell, or a cell with its frame switched off.

The page is calm and flat, and the eye goes to two things. One is the plot, which shows the take as a white burst inside a radial hairline grid. The other is a single red mark: the entry being recorded now, or the armed end of the Record cell. Everything else stays white on black at three ink strengths. Density changes with window size, but the world doesn't. The phone follows the approved comp exactly, measured in comp pixels and scaled by one unit `u`. Wide windows set the same parts side by side, with the catalogue index as a left column.
keyCharacteristics: Matte black ground, ink in three strengths, hairline rules at 1 px, square corners everywhere except the round plot.
Two faces only: Geist (light, for the words people write and display numerals) and Geist Mono (light to medium, for everything engraved, numbered or measured).
One red, reserved for what is live now.
Each song's colour code strip is the only place that uses colour as decoration, and it is data.
Motion is one grammar. Things step in with an exponential ease-out and nothing bounces. Reduce-motion makes everything static.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Outside the code strip, red means "live now": the entry being recorded, the armed end of the primary action, or a fault mark. It is never a decoration, a hover state or a category colour. Failed and stopped entries go to muted ink.

rules.name: The Code Is Data Rule
rules.body: The colour code is derived from the song's seed and drawn only as a strip. Never take a code colour for chrome, text or state.

rules.name: The Eleven Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing set in this world drops below 11 logical px, at any scale.

rules.name: The Two Hands Rule
rules.body: The mono engraves (labels, numbers, measurements, actions) and Geist light writes (the user's words). Never set user-written text in mono or a label in Geist.

rules.name: The Shared Rule Rule
rules.body: A horizontal rule that crosses the index column and the page must sit at the same height on both sides: 124 px on the studio, 64 px on secondary pages.

rules.name: The Comp Authority Rule
rules.body: Below 600 px, a layout question goes to the comp, expressed in comp px times `u`, and is never invented afresh.

rules.name: The Printed Sleeve Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If something needs separating, give it a rule or a band, never a shadow, a glow or a lighter card.

dos: **Do** build every control from the hairline cell (1 px, radius 0, 48 px minimum target) and change only its frame colour for state: rule at rest, ink when selected, red when live.
**Do** measure phone layouts in comp px times `u` and defer to the comp below 600 px.
**Do** keep the 124 px studio header band and the 64 px page header so rules line up across the index column.
**Do** set user-written words in Geist 300 and everything engraved in Geist Mono with 0.16em tracking, uppercase, never below 11 px.
**Do** step things in at 260 ms on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` and honour reduce-motion by rendering the final state.
**Do** draw new glyphs on the 24-unit grid with a 1.25 px square-capped stroke.
donts: **Don't** use red for anything except the live entry, the armed primary block and fault marks. Failed or stopped states use muted ink.
**Don't** use code-strip colours outside a code strip.
**Don't** round a rectangle, add a shadow or glow, or lift a surface to a lighter card. The plot's circle is the only curve.
**Don't** add stock Material components (filled buttons, chips, outlined text fields, FABs, ripples). The theme turns splash and highlight off.
